subject.title: feat: unify external sessions with native catalog pagination

question: Should external session catalog metadata and transcript reads use `operator.read`, with continuation and archive reserved for `operator.write`, and should an existing explicit `supervision.enabled: false` continue to suppress the Codex catalog after upgrade?
rationale: The PR changes both authorization and an explicit persisted consent setting; code inspection identifies the safest compatibility-preserving default, but maintainers must confirm the permanent product and security boundary.

options.title: Preserve consent and split scopes
options.body: Keep explicit false authoritative for catalog visibility, authorize list/read with `operator.read`, and keep continue/archive on `operator.write`.

options.title: Migrate consent, split scopes
options.body: Deliberately redefine explicit false as tool-only through a documented doctor migration while still separating read and write scopes.

options.title: Require write scope for all
options.body: Expose catalogs whenever the plugin is active and require `operator.write` even for browsing, accepting both upgrade and read-only-user breakage.

recommendation.title: Preserve consent and split scopes
recommendation.body: Keep explicit false authoritative for catalog visibility, authorize list/read with `operator.read`, and keep continue/archive on `operator.write`.

likelyOwner.reason: This identity introduced and currently owns the unified session-catalog direction across the affected product and runtime surfaces.
